hypotheses.text: Seizures (HP:0001250) occur in approximately 80% of individuals with GTF3C3-related neurodevelopmental disorder overall, but frequency varies significantly by cohort (from 50% in small cohorts to >80% in pooled reviews).
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifying the exact penetrance of seizures is crucial for diagnostic clinical suspicion; Abdel et al. found seizures in 2/4 (50%) individuals, whereas López's comprehensive review documented seizures in 14/17 (82.35%) individuals.

evidence.text: In a comprehensive review of reported GTF3C3 cases, seizures were present in 14 of 17 assessed individuals (82.35%) with variable types including tonic, clonic, and absence seizures.

hypotheses.text: Corpus callosum anomalies (agenesis or hypoplasia, HP:0001274 / HP:0002079) are present in fewer than half (40-45%) of evaluated individuals with GTF3C3 variants, indicating that an intact corpus callosum does not rule out the disorder.
hypotheses.rationale: While corpus callosum malformations are frequently cited as a core feature of GTF3C3 neurodevelopmental disorder, exact counting across literature indicates it is not fully penetrant.

evidence.text: In the comprehensive review cohort, structural anomalies of the corpus callosum were documented in 7 of 16 evaluated patients (43.75%).

hypotheses.text: Secondary cortical malformations such as simplified gyral pattern (HP:0009879) are rare findings present in <30% of GTF3C3 patients, representing severe end-spectrum neuroimaging features rather than sensitive diagnostic hallmarks.
hypotheses.rationale: Differentiating primary or frequent findings (like cerebellar hypoplasia or corpus callosum anomalies) from infrequent findings (simplified gyral pattern) allows clinicians to avoid misclassification.

evidence.text: Brain imaging demonstrated brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement across patients, while moderate to severe simplified gyral pattern was seen in only 1 of 4 patients.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact numerators and denominators for motor abnormalities, specifically spasticity and dystonia, across the De Hayr et al. (12 patients) and ESHG cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: De Hayr et al. and the ESHG abstracts highlight motor impairments, spasticity, and dystonia as associated features, but the exact frequency counts in the full cohorts need systematic compilation.

new_directions.question_text: What is the pooled frequency of microcephaly (HP:0000252) when aggregating the De Hayr (12 patients), Abdel (4 patients), and López review cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Microcephaly is stated in OMIM #621201 and Abdel et al. as a core feature, but checking whether it is consistently present across all reported cohorts will clarify its sensitivity as a diagnostic criterion.
